'''''Solanum wendlandii''''', the '''giant potato creeper''', '''potato vine''', '''Costa Rican nightshade''', '''divorce vine''', or '''paradise flower''', is a species of flowering plant in the family [[Solanaceae]]. It is native to Mexico, Central America, and northwest South America, and has been widely introduced as an ornamental to other tropical locales, including the Caribbean, Africa, Nepal, Java, and many islands in the Indian and Pacific Oceans.<ref name="240016-2" >{{cite POWO |id=240016-2 |title=''Solanum wendlandii'' Hook.f. |access-date=8 December 2021 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=''Solanum wendlandii'' giant potato creeper |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/17458/i-solanum-wendlandii-i/details |date=2021 |publisher=The Royal Horticultural Society |access-date=8 December 2021 }}</ref> A robust vine reaching {{cvt|15|ft|m}}, its long-lasting dark purple flowers eventually fade to white.<ref>{{cite web |title=Giant Potato Creeper |url=https://www.flowersofindia.net/catalog/slides/Giant%20Potato%20Creeper.html |date=2021 |publisher=Flowers of India |access-date=8 December 2021 }}</ref>
